messages:
maria: quick heads-up — I'm sketching a small design to avoid dual-serving and stale-writes during rolling restarts of cache workers. idea: ephemeral ownership token + short reconciliation window + probe-on-read to repair stale prefixes. want quick feedback on correctness tradeoffs and metrics we should track.

oliver: +1 on token + probe. couple Qs: how do tokens get ordered? if two nodes issue tokens concurrently we need a deterministic tie-breaker (epoch + node id). also thinking about whether writes should be allowed while token is contested.

raj: concern: hotkey migration. if we allow reads from non-owners (borrow) we might accidentally create split-brain for writes. maybe allow reads-only borrow, and writes must be pinned to the current owner or forwarded. how expensive is forward-to-owner latency-wise?

mina: idea: borrow fast-path for reads only, include provenance header so the caller knows response came from a borrower (for correctness/telemetry). schedule async takeover: borrower tries to acquire ownership quietly if it sees sustained traffic. demotion should be a waterfall not kill — demote score -> soft-evict -> hard-evict.

sam: metrics to add: counters for borrowed_reads, probe_on_read_hits, ownership_conflicts, takeover_attempts, takeover_success_rate, demote_steps_count. also record histograms for borrower latency vs direct owner latency. these help decide grace window sizes.

infra-bot: canary note: last canary with borrow enabled saw borrowed_reads=1.2k, probe_on_read_hits=48, p99 latency +0.2%.

maria: rough pseudo for handshake / reconciliation I'm thinking (very small):

```
# on startup / restart
token = {epoch: local_epoch++, node: NODE_ID, nonce: rand()}
publish_token(prefix, token)
wait(reconcile_window)
if see_higher_token(prefix): relinquish_ownership()
else become_owner(prefix, token)

# on read if not owner:
if borrower_allowed(prefix): reply_from_borrower(with_provenance=true)
schedule_background_takeover_attempt(prefix)
# probe: fetch owner.last_applied_seq for prefix and compare; if stale, trigger repair
```

oliver: I like the explicit higher-token check. add invariant: writes only by current canonical owner (token that wins tiebreaker). reads allowed by borrower but must tag responses. that keeps linearizability for writes. we should also add an explicit tombstone/transfer record so takeover is auditable.

raj: test plan item: simulate dual-start where node A and B both believe they own prefix for 10s. assert no lost writes and no out-of-order commit. deterministic tiebreaker test: epoch+nodeid. also test heavy-hotkey migration with borrower ramp to ensure cost isn't doubled.

mina: I'll run a microbenchmark: 5k qps hotkey, restart owner every 30s, measure borrowed_reads ratio and p50/p99. also will try failure injection where takeover half-succeeds.

sam: ops action: add telemetry dashboards for the new metrics and an alert if borrowed_reads > 0.5% of total for >5min. also a chase metric for takeover_failure_rate.

maria: action items summary: 1) mina spike + microbench, 2) raj write the deterministic-tiebreaker unit tests + chaos harness, 3) oliver draft short RFC with invariants and transfer record format, 4) sam add dashboards/alerts, 5) infra-bot: schedule canary after spike. will draft RFC by EOW.

deploy-bot: canary scheduled for 03:00 UTC tomorrow against staging cluster :rocket:

maria: thanks all — keeping this lightweight so we can iterate. if anyone sees a correctness hole call it out now or in the RFC. :thumbsup:
